**In Praise of Tuesday**

If I get to write about absolutely anything, I want to write about Tuesday.

Monday gets all the poetry. It's slamming snooze buttons and spilling coffee and dramatic sighs. Friday gets the fireworks. Saturday gets the lie-ins, Sunday gets the slow fade. Tuesday just quietly shows up in a plain sweater with no meme attached to it, and gets on with things.

And honestly? Tuesday is where life actually happens.

Monday is a performance. You make the list, you announce the list, you buy a new planner with gold foil on it. Tuesday is when you discover if you actually believe your own list. It's the first real test. Did you go to the gym? Probably not. Did you write the email? Maybe. Did you eat the vegetables you bought with such optimism? Well, you at least opened the fridge and looked at them with respectful recognition.

Tuesday is the hinge day. The world has stopped pretending it's a fresh start and it hasn't yet started pretending it's almost the weekend. It's just... Thursday's cousin, Wednesday's younger sibling, stubbornly in the middle of everything. It's the day you fold the laundry because it's been sitting in the basket long enough to qualify as furniture. It's the day you finally call the dentist. It's the day you go to the grocery store for "just milk" and come home with milk, a melon you didn't plan for, and a vague sense of accomplishment.

I love Tuesday light. It's not golden like Friday evening. It's not pale like Monday morning. Tuesday light is Tuesday light — fluorescent in office buildings, a little grey through kitchen windows, sincere. If it's raining on a Tuesday, it's just raining. No one's writing songs about it. The rain just does its job and you get wet and you get home and you make tea and that feels like a small, uncelebrated victory.

Tuesday is also when people are kindest, I think. Not in the big holiday way. In the small way. The bus driver waits two seconds longer. Your coworker remembers how you take your coffee. A stranger holds the elevator. Nobody's out of patience yet, nobody's checked out yet. We're in the thick of it, together, doing the ordinary work of being alive.

I have a theory that Tuesdays are better for starting things than Mondays. Mondays are too loud. Tuesday is the day you quietly decide: okay, I'm going to learn to make decent soup. I'm going to read twenty pages a night. I'm going to text that friend back. Not because it's a new year, not because it's symbolic, but because on Tuesday you ran out of excuses. You tried the grand gesture on Monday and it peeled off by 10 a.m. Now only the real thing remains.

And Tuesdays have the best potential for tiny miracles. A song you forgot you loved comes on in a cafe. Someone leaves an umbrella in the library and you inherit it. You find a note in your coat pocket from last winter that just says "you've got this" in your own handwriting and you have absolutely no memory of writing it. That's Tuesday magic. No thunder. Just a small glow.

So here's to Tuesday: to library cards renewed, to leftovers eaten with gratitude, to midweek check-ins, to doing the dishes before they become a mountain. To the ordinary, unphotogenic, stubbornly wonderful middle of the weekderful.

May your Tuesday be unremarkable in the best possible way.
